business_scope.primary_industry_name: Overseas Direct-Operated Hotpot Dining and Condiment Supply

Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation (2016)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Control Act (Taiwan, most recently consolidated in 2016 and amended through 2018); Enforcement Rules of the Money Laundering Control Act; Company Act Article 22-1 (Beneficial Ownership Registration); Regulations on the Registration of Company Beneficial Owners (2018); Counter-Terrorism Financing Act (2016); and the Investment Regulations by Mainland Chinese Investors, administered by the Investment Commission, MOEA.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the sole foreign investing company (or of the immediate corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation, People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait Document Verification (administrative legalization through SEAS/ARATS); the Hague Apostille Convention is not applied by Taiwan to PRC-origin documents, so consular legalization remains the operative path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the investing corporate chain (including all amendments)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR / Relevant PRC Registry Authority and Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait Document Verification (SEAS/ARATS notarization and legalization pathway).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate ownership structure chart and Beneficial Ownership Declaration identifying all natural persons holding 25% or more of the investment chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investing company management board authenticated by a PRC Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait Document Verification and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing the establishment of the Taiwan subsidiary, appointing its first legal representative/director, and approving the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the investing company (notarized in PRC)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Taiwan incorporation agent, licensed attorney, or certified public accountant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investing company; authenticated before a PRC Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait Document Verification and subsequent acceptance by the MOEA One-Stop Service.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence screening against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, EU and UK sanctions, and the Taiwan Financial Intelligence Unit's domestic sanctions and PEP databases. For each natural person owning 25% or more of the ownership chain, counsel must verify identity, source of funds, and politically exposed person status, including all immediate family members and close associates where applicable. As this is a mainland-Chinese investment into Taiwan, enhanced due diligence is required under the MOEA Investment Commission's review standards, including verification of the mainland investor's permitted business scope and compliance with cross-strait investment approval requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs Company and Commerce Registration One-Stop Service (公司與商業一站式線上申請作業)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal company name must be in Chinese characters. An English trade name is optional but, if adopted, must be filed separately and must not create confusion with existing registered names. Romanization/pinyin transliteration of the Chinese name may be approved where the foreign trade name is required for the international restaurant brand.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 任何暗示政府機構、金融特許業務、公眾福利或公益性之名稱
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notification issued through the MOEA One-Stop Service, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days of receipt. The appeal must be addressed to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and set out the grounds of non-confusion, actual business distinction, or legal authorization to use the prohibited token. The applicant may alternatively submit a revised name application electronically without prejudice to the appeal. A reserved name may be extended once for an additional 180 days before incorporation only where the applicant demonstrates ongoing preparation and pays the statutory extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for the hotpot restaurant trade. A physical, directly operated dining premises with food and beverage business registration, kitchen/food-handling facilities, and fire safety compliance is mandatory. A virtual office may be utilized only for administrative correspondence and ancillary back-office activities, but it cannot satisfy the registered office or commercial substance requirements of the Taiwan Company Act or the food business licensing regime.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 95% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation, conducted by the Taiwan Department/Municipal Health Bureau for food safety and by the Fire Bureau for fire-prevention standards; additional checks may be triggered by the MOEA Investment Commission during the establishment phase.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, particularly Articles 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 18, 128, 129, 131, 156, 163, 170, 172, 177, 183, 192, 195, 202, 208, 216, 218 and 387; Business Registration Act; Foreign Investment Approval Act; Taiwan Area and Mainland Area Relations Act and the Regulations Governing Permission of Trade and Investment between the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area. A PRC-invested entity cannot use the ordinary Taiwan foreign-investment route without the applicable Mainland-investment approvals. Wholly foreign-owned enterprise is not a standalone Taiwan legal form; the vehicle should ordinarily be a Taiwan company limited by shares or limited company.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, together with the competent municipal or county/city government economic development or commercial registration department for the registered office location. PRC-origin investment must also be reviewed by the Investment Review Department, Ministry of Economic Affairs, under the applicable Mainland-investment rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration, accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation, shareholder or incorporator documentation, capital verification documents, registered-office consent, director and supervisor or auditor appointment documents, and foreign or Mainland investment approval documentation where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan generally has no universal statutory minimum paid-up capital for an ordinary company. Capital must be sufficient for the proposed business and must be fully subscribed and paid before registration. A bank escrow account is not generally mandatory; capital is normally remitted to a temporary or company bank account and verified by a Taiwan certified public accountant. Foreign or Mainland investment capital must follow the approved investment amount, remittance, reporting, and foreign-exchange procedures. The stated filing fee is an approximate United States dollar equivalent of the standard electronic company-registration fee and should be confirmed in New Taiwan dollars at filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts the subscription for its issued shares by the approved subscriber in the amount and consideration stated in the incorporation documents, subject to receipt and verification of the subscription funds; (2) the registered office at the approved address is adopted; (3) [Name] is appointed Chairperson, [Name] is appointed General Manager, and [Name] is appointed responsible food-service and compliance officer, each subject to applicable law; (4) the responsible officer is authorized to complete company registration, tax registration, bank-account opening, investment-capital remittance, food-business registration, fire-safety, building-use, and environmental filings; and (5) all prior acts consistent with these resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Investor Eligibility and Business-Scope Permission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Review Department, Ministry of Economic Affairs; Mainland Affairs Council where consultation or policy review is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the PRC parent, its beneficial owners, or any Mainland-controlled entity is the investor. Do not file as an ordinary foreign investor if the investment is Mainland-origin. Obtain the required Mainland-investment permission before capital remittance or commencement of business. Confirm that hotpot dining, condiment supply, retail, franchising, and related activities are permitted for the proposed investor and location.
required_dossiers: Investor constitutional documents and certificates of incorporation
Ownership chart to ultimate beneficial owners
Audited financial statements or proof of financial capacity
Certified Chinese translations and Taiwan authentication or legalization, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to information requests within the prescribed period, correct the investment classification, amend the business scope, and file an administrative appeal or petition for reconsideration if a formal adverse decision is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Check System of the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Chinese and English company names and the precise business activities. Use the relevant Taiwan business codes for restaurant operations, food and condiment trading, and any import, retail, or catering activities. Confirm that the registered premises may be used for food-service operations before finalizing the lease.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace conflicting names, remove restricted business items, or resubmit the amended application. Preserve the approved name within its validity period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Constitutional Documents and Appoint Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company registration authority for the registered-office location; notary public where notarization is required by the document or foreign-investor procedure
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Articles of Incorporation, subscription or capital-contribution instruments, director and supervisor or auditor consents, registered-office consent, and power of attorney. Authenticate foreign or Mainland documents through the applicable Taiwan representative office, notary, certification, or legalization channel. Appoint the responsible person and comply with director nationality and residence documentation requirements.
required_dossiers: Director, supervisor, auditor, and responsible-person consent letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure missing signatures, authentication defects, translation defects, or officer eligibility issues and re-execute the affected instruments before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Capital Account, Remit Funds, and Obtain CPA Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan commercial bank, Central Bank foreign-exchange channel, and Taiwan certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the designated capital account after investment approval. Remit the approved capital through the banking system using the approved investor and purpose codes. Obtain bank remittance evidence and a CPA capital verification report. Do not use unapproved third-party funding or commence operations before the required capital and investment filings are complete.
required_dossiers: Capital verification engagement and CPA report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct remitter identity, purpose codes, or remittance amount; obtain bank and regulatory confirmation; and file supplemental foreign-exchange or investment reports where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Company Registration and Obtain Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent municipal or county/city government commercial-registration department, with central processing or supervision by the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company-registration application electronically or in paper form with the approved name, Articles of Incorporation, officer documents, registered-office evidence, CPA capital report, investment approval, and government fee. Ensure the registered office, business scope, paid-in capital, and responsible person exactly match the approved materials.
required_dossiers: Director and supervisor or auditor appointment documents
Foreign or Mainland investor authentication documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the registry query by the stated deadline, submit corrected documents and explanations, pay any additional fee, and request re-review. A formal refusal may be challenged through administrative appeal or litigation under Taiwan administrative procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Labor, Banking, and Beneficial-Owner Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau branch; local labor authority; designated bank; competent commercial-registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the tax account and business-tax status, confirm uniform invoice requirements, activate the corporate bank account, enroll eligible employees in labor insurance and health insurance, establish payroll withholding, and maintain statutory accounting books. Report post-registration capital and investment changes within the applicable deadlines.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or labor registration data, file late registrations with explanations, pay statutory interest or penalties where assessed, and request a tax or labor authority review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Restaurant, Food, Building, Fire, and Environmental Approvals Before Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal or county/city government economic development, health, building, environmental protection, and fire departments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify zoning and approved building use for restaurant operations. Complete food-business registration, obtain any required food-service or import approvals, secure fire-safety inspection approval, install compliant grease interception, ventilation, exhaust, gas, electrical, and wastewater systems, and obtain environmental permits if emissions, wastewater, waste, or construction thresholds apply. Do not open to the public until all location-specific approvals are complete.
required_dossiers: Gas, electrical, exhaust, and ventilation certificates
Employee health and food-handler records where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies identified in inspection reports, submit revised drawings, request reinspection, and appeal or seek administrative reconsideration of a formal refusal. Suspend opening or affected operations until approval is obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The local municipal or county/city government economic development department for commercial registration and food premises, coordinated with the local public health bureau, building administration office, fire department, and environmental protection bureau. Taiwan does not generally issue a single nationwide manufacturing-style industrial license for an ordinary restaurant.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration Certificate together with Food Business Registration or Food-Service Business Registration, as required by the local public health authority. Separate approvals may apply to food importation, packaged condiment production, alcohol service, signage, outdoor seating, or waste transport.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Ministry of Environment, Taiwan, and the competent local environmental protection bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a formal Environmental Impact Assessment for a conventional restaurant operating within an existing legally approved commercial building, subject to site, construction, scale, development, and sensitive-area thresholds. A project involving major construction, redevelopment, a designated environmentally sensitive area, or a prescribed scale may require an EIA screening and, if triggered, a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Water Pollution Control Act and local discharge requirements for wastewater, including grease interception, pretreatment, sanitary wastewater, and any required discharge permit. Comply with the Air Pollution Control Act and local nuisance-control rules for kitchen exhaust, smoke, odor, particulate matter, and VOCs. Store, classify, contract for removal, and document food waste, used cooking oil, grease-trap waste, packaging, and hazardous chemicals under the Waste Disposal Act. No universal restaurant-wide numerical VOC or wastewater threshold applies without reference to the discharge route, permit category, local sewer rules, and applicable standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening, obtain or pass the applicable fire-safety review and inspection covering evacuation routes, fire compartments, alarms, extinguishers, emergency lighting, exits, gas systems, kitchen suppression, and occupancy load. Confirm building-use compliance, structural loading, electrical and gas safety, ventilation, and exhaust approvals with the local building authority. Comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including risk assessments, employee training, machine and kitchen-equipment safeguards, chemical handling, accident reporting, and labor-inspection requirements. Public-access premises may require periodic fire and equipment inspections.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Information Report (Company Act Art. 22-1) — directors, managers, and shareholding data for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce — Company and Commerce Registration System (online)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed annual window: 1 January – 31 January immediately following the preceding calendar year; holidays extend to the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA notice followed by a cure period; fines of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 (USD 310–1,560) per violation; repeated failure may lead to compulsory execution and ultimately an administrative dissolution or strike-off action by MOEA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Operation Report for Foreign-Invested Enterprise — annual confirmation of business operations of the Taiwanese WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year WFOE: no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger rejection of future investment applications, administrative warnings, and fines under the investment statutes; prolonged non-compliance may impair the WFOE's registration status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Business Report — approval by shareholders and preservation at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No standing filing required; retained at registered office and submitted promptly to MOEA, National Taxation Bureau, or competent authority upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end; calendar-year WFOE: no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officers and directors may be fined NT$20,000–NT$100,000 (USD 625–3,125) for failure to prepare or adopt financial statements; continued non-compliance may permit regulators to compel production through administrative enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) — local district tax office having jurisdiction over the WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window 1 May – 31 May following the calendar tax year; CPA-audited returns may submit supplement documents by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge equal to 10% of unpaid tax if filed within 3 months after the ordinary deadline, and 20% if filed later, plus monthly interest on unpaid amounts; prolonged non-payment can trigger liens, garnishments, and enforced collection without administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent CPA audit applies when paid-in capital reaches the MOEA-published threshold of NT$30 million (approximately USD 950,000); audit may also be required by banks, creditors, or the National Taxation Bureau for regulatory review, even if the capital threshold is not met
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TW FRS) converged with IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission; non-public limited companies below the FSC designation may apply the lower-complexity Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS) for financial statement preparation

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual Company Act Art. 22-1 report operates as the annual UBO confirmation; direct shareholding changes and indirect ultimate beneficial ownership changes must be filed with MOEA online within 15 days of the event, and the on-site shareholders' register must be physically updated before the annual statutory confirmation is signed

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: NT$80,000–NT$150,000 (approximately USD 2,500–4,700) for a WFOE meeting audit requirements; no audit fee below the statutory threshold
